chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding sleeping in the mosques?' He said, 'There is no harm in it, except in the two mosques: the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sacred Mosque.'

He said, 'And he used to take my hand in some part of the night, so he would sit in a corner, then sit down and converse in the Sacred Mosque. So sometimes he slept, and I slept. So I spoke to him regarding that, so he said, 'It is only disliked to sleep in the Sacred Mosque which was in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). But as for sleeping in this place, there is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep in the mosques according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general permissibility of sleeping in mosques and the specific reverence due to the two holiest sanctuaries, noting that the prohibition primarily applied to the original structure of the Sacred Mosque during the Prophet's era. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly nuance in distinguishing between the physical location and its historical sanctity, allowing for practical accommodation in the current expanded structures while maintaining respect for the Prophet's Mosque and the Kaaba's immediate precincts. It underscores the principle that sleeping in mosques is not inherently impeding unless it disrespects the specific sanctity of these key sites.
